title: State of Washington v. Thorne
questions: Whether the "three strikes" law (Initiative 593) was enacted in violation of Const. art. II, sec 37 by failing to set forth the statutes amended, or violates substantive or procedural due process, the separation of powers doctrine, or the constitutional prohibitions against cruel punishment.

title: State of Washington v. Rivers
questions: Whether the "three strikes" law (Initiative 593) was enacted in violation of Const. art. II, sec 37 by failing to set forth the statutes amended, or violates substantive or procedural due process, the separation of powers doctrine, or the constitutional prohibitions against cruel punishment.

title: Brown v. State of Washington
questions: Whether the State of Washington or landowners adjacent to parcels formerly used by the Milwaukee Railroad now own those parcels, where the State claims ownership based on a 1981 purchase from the railroad's bankruptcy trustee, and the adjacent landowners claim ownership through bandonment and reversion.

title: State of Washington v. Manussier
questions: Petitioner challenges the constitutionality of Initiative 593, codified in RCW 9.94A.120(4) and commonly referred to as the "three strikes law," which imposes a mandatory life sentence without possibility of parole upon conviction of a third "most serious offense".

title: State of Washington v. Maupin
questions: Whether the trial court erroneously excluded testimony by a witness who claimed to have seen the victim, after she was abducted, with a man other than the defendant.

title: Peninsula School District No. 401 v. Public School Employees
questions: Whether job security provisions in a collective bargaining agreement are enforceable beyond a classified public school employees statutory one-year term of employment.

title: U.S. Life Credit Life Insurance v. Williams
questions: Whether extrinisic evidence of the meaning of certain marks on a certificate of credit life insurance, obtained when purchasing a vehicle, created an issue of fact as to the parties' intent regarding converage for both purchasing spouses.

title: Griffin v. Eller
questions: Whether the Law Against Discrimination, RCW 49.60, authorizes private employment discrimination actions against employers of fewer than eight persons, and if not, whether this limitation violates the privileges and immunities clause of the state constitution.

title: State of Washington v. Wakefield
questions: Whether a defendant must be sentenced within the standard range because she pleaded guilty after the trial court said that if she did so she would receive a standard range sentence.

title: State of Washington v. LeFaber
questions: Whether the self-defense instruction in this homicide prosecution incorrectly told the jury that homicide is justifiable in self-defense only if there is an actual imminent danger of harm being inflicted on the defendant or another.

title: State of Washington Lisa Johnson & Theresa Fricke v. Sarun Chhom Michael Trickey Whether rape of a child
Peter C. Albert James Rosenberger v. Morris Piha Management Group
State ex rel. T.B. v. CPC Fairfax Hospital
questions: Whether the amendments to RCW 71.34 made by Laws of 1995 ch. 313 (the "Becca Bill") permit a 15-year-old to be admitted to a mental health facility on her parents' request and be detained without judicial hearing despite her demand for discharge, and if so, whether the statutory scheme violates the Constitution.

title: State of Washington v. Crediford
questions: Appellant challenges the constitutionality of the 1993 version of RCW 46.61.502(1), which prohibits operation of a vehicle by a driver whose blood alcohol concentration measures .10 or greater within two hours after driving.

title: Moe v. Hansen
questions: Whether a widower's prenuptial agreement with his deceased spouse prevents him from getting his "ommitted spouse" share of her estate.

title: In re Personal Restraint of Fleming
Presidential Estates Apartment Associates, et al. v.
questions: Whether amendments to a judgment involved only clerical mistakes arising from the trial judge's oversight or omission, thus satisfying the requirements of Civil Rule 60(a).

title: Findlay v. United Pacific Insurance
questions: Whether a homeowner's insurance policy provision violates the efficient proximate cause rule by excluding coverage of losses caused by weather conditions when combined with earth movement.

title: State of Washington v. Chhom
questions: Whether rape of a child, which does not include intent as an element, can support a charge of criminal attempt.

title: State of Washington v. Bolar
questions: Whether in sentencing a defendant whose record includes three or more prior offenses for which he served concurrent sentences, the court in computing the offender score may aggregate some but not all of the prior offenses. See RCW 9.94A.360(6)(a).
result: petitioning party received a favorable disposition

title: State of Washington v. Ross
questions: Whether a guilty plea is invalid if the defendant is unaware that the crime carries a mandatory period of community placement in addition to any prison term.

title: State of Washington v. Heiskell
questions: Whether the juvenile court, upon convicting a juvenile under 15 of a sex offense, has discretion under RCW 9A.44.140(2) and (3) to exempt the juvenile from sex-offender registration within two years of the conviction.

title: Young v. Key Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
questions: Whether a prescription drug manufacturer can be held strictly liable for failure to warn of dangers of its product, or must the plaintiff show that the failure to warn was negligent.

title: Stuckey v. Department of Labor & Industries
questions: Whether the Department of Labor & Industries, in recouping partial disability lump sum payments after claimants appealed and were awarded permanent disability pensions, must deduct the erroneously paid amount from the claimants' pension reserves or may instead reduce future payments to the claimants.

title: Stiley v. Block
questions: Whether the Court of Appeals erred in reversing a jury verdict for fraud, legal malpractice, and breach of contract based on errors in jury instructions, erroneous use of a statute to impeach the defendant, and insufficiency of evidence to prove fraud.

title: State of Washington v. L.J.M.
questions: Whether the trial court in this jury trial correctly found sufficient proof that the crime, which was committed within the boundaries of the Colville Reservation, occurred on fee land and was thus within state court jurisdiction..

title: State of Washington v. Hardesty
questions: After a person completes his or her jail sentence, can the State constitutionally send him back to jail because he should have been given a longer sentence?

title: Griffith v. City of Bellevue
questions: Whether the trial court lacked jurisdiction to review a city land use decision because the petition filed with the court was unverified, even though the copy served on the city had a signed verification.

title: Osborn v. Grant County
questions: Whether the Grant County Board of Commissioners unlawfully interfered with the county clerk's authority to hire employees, and whether the clerk had standing to bring suit to challenge the board's action and the right to appointment of a special prosecutor to represent her.

title: State of Washington v. White
questions: Whether the police needed a warrant to arrest a suspected felon in a toilet stall of a public restroom.

title: Edgar v. City of Tacoma
questions: Whether RCW 4.22.070(1), as amended by Laws of 1993, ch. 496, which excludes immune employers as entities to whom fault may be assigned, impairs the constitutional right to jury trial.

title: Cary v. Allstate Insurance
questions: Whether an exclusion clause in a homeowner's insurance policy denying coverage for acts committed by an insured while insane violates public policy and thus should not be enforced?

title: State of Washington v. King
questions: Was the defendant's Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination violated when disclosures he made at Western State Hospital during court-ordered treatment were used to support his exceptional minimum term sentence?

title: State of Washington v. Tunney
questions: Whether an information charging third degree assault of a police officer under RCW 9A.36.031(1)(g) is constitutionally defective if it does not allege the defendant knew the victim was performing official duties at the time of the alleged assault.

title: Seattle Seahawks, Inc. v. King County
questions: Whether, for purposes of obtaining trial court jurisdiction over the controversy, a cause of action is commenced by (i) filing of the complain, or (ii) service of the summons and complaint, and filing of the complaint.

title: Dailey v. North Coast Life Insurance
questions: Whether punitive damages, which were authorized by a 1991 amendment to the federal Civil Rights Act, are available in this employment discrimination action, which was brought under state law and arose out of a termination that occurred in 1990.

title: Sheldon v. Fettig
questions: Whether the defendant, who was then living principally in Chicago, was properly served at the "house of [her] usual abode" when copies of the summons and complaint were left at her parents' home in Seattle.

title: Felt v. McCarthy
questions: Whether the doctrine of supervening frustration excuses a real estate developer from making further payments due under a real estate contract because wetlands legislation has rendered the property unsuitable for development.

title: State of Washington v. Aten
questions: Whether, in this manslaughter prosecution, a pathologist's testimony that the victim's respiratory failure could have been caused by suffocation provided sufficient independent evidence of the corpus delicti of the crime to permit the admission of the defendant's statements and confession.

title: CLEAN v. State of Washington
questions: Whether EHB 2115 (Laws of 1995, 3d Ex. Sess., ch. 1), which authorizes funding sources for the construction of a major league baseball stadium in King County, is void because of an invalid "emergency clause," or violates constitutional prohibitions against gifts of public funds, lending public credit, or special legislation.

title: Clallam County v. Folk
questions: Whether a county may foreclose on a delinquent taxpayer's fractional undivided interest in a parcel of real property without notifying the owners of the other undivided interests in that parcel.

title: Richmond v. Thompson
questions: Whether a person who makes a complaint to the Governor's Office about the official conduct of a state trooper is immune from liability for defamation for any maliciously false statements contained in the complaint.

title: Jain v. State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance
questions: Whether Tissell v. Liberty Mut. Ins. Co., 115 Wn.2d 107, 795 P.2d 126 (1990) should be applied retroactively to void a release previously given by the plaintiff to her insurer. See Bradbury v. Aetna Cas. & Sur. Co., 91 Wn.2d 505, 589 P.2d 785 (1979).

title: State of Washington v. Eastmond
questions: Whether an instruction can be challenged initially on appeal on the ground that it gives an erroneous definition of one of the elements of a crime and, if so, whether the definition of "assault" given here was erroneous.

title: State of Washington v. Stewart
questions: Whether a defendant's right to a speedy trial under the criminal rules is violated when the State does not extradite the defendant from another state for trial, and does not comply with a court order to set a new trial date.

title: State of Washington v. Branch
questions: Whether a defendant should be permitted to withdraw his guilty plea because he did not sign the statement of defendant on plea of guilty.

title: State of Washington v. Hudson
questions: Whether under CrR 3.3 and State v. Strike, 87 Wn.2d 870, 557 P.2d 847 (1976), an out-of-state defendant can be "amendable to process," requiring the State to excercise due deligence in securing his presence.

title: State of Washington v. Harris
questions: Whether a defendant's right to a speedy trial on a felony charge was violated by the State's failure to file that charge with an earlier charge arising out of the same criminal episode.

title: State of Washington v. Smith
questions: Whether the results of a BAC Verifier DataMaster test of the defendant's breath alcohol level should be suppressed because the arresting officer first administered a breath test with an unapproved portable machine and failed to preserve the results of that test.

title: Clauson v. Department of Labor & Industries
questions: Whether a worker who receives an industrial insurance pension for permanent total disability may later receive an award for permanent partial disability based on a separate, preexisting injury.

title: Bodin v. City of Stanwood
questions: Whether, in this action against a city for damages caused by an overflowing sewer lagoon, the trial court properly admitted evidence of the city's efforts to procure federal funds to pay for raising the dikes surrounding the lagoon.

title: Anderson & Middleton Lumber Co. v. Quinault Indian Nation
questions: Whether a state court has jurisdiction over a suit to partition land located on the Quinault Indian Reservation owned by a private corporation and the Quinault Indian Nation.

title: Seattle Building & Construction Trades Council v. Apprenticeship & Training Council
questions: Whether registration of an apprenticeship program by the Washington State Apprenticeship and Training Council is a "license" for purposes of the Administrative Procedure Act, thus requiring the Council to hold an adjudicative hearing if the registration is contested.

title: State of Washington v. Easter
questions: Whether the State may use as substantive evidence of guilt a defendant's silence when questioned by officers following an automobile accident.

title: State of Washington v. Lewis
questions: Whether the State may use a criminal defendant's pre-arrest silence as substantive evidence of guilt in the prosecution's case in chief.

title: Health Insurance Pool v. Health Care Authority
questions: Whether the Washington Health Care Authority, as administrator of the state employees' Uniform Medical Plan, is a "member" of the Washington State Health Insurance Pool and thus must pay assessments charged to members.

title: K.C. v. Department of Social & Health Services
questions: Under RCW 13.34, did the State adequately prove the allegations supporting orders terminating the parent-child relationships in this case?
result: petitioning party received a favorable disposition

title: State of Washington v. Werner
questions: Whether a superior court judge not explicitly sitting as a juvenile court judge has authority to issue an arrest warrant for a juvenile and, if not, whether the seizure of a marijuana grow operation in the defendant's home was the fruit of his juvenile stepson's unlawful arrest.
result: petitioning party received a favorable disposition

title: State of Washington v. Ray
questions: Whether, in this prosecution for child molestation, there is sufficient evidence of the corpus delicti to allow admission of the defendant's statements.

title: State of Washington v. Clark
questions: Whether placing a death penalty notice in the box at the prosecutor's office used for pickup and delivery of correspondence with the public defender constituted proper service of the notice on defendant's counsel.

title: State of Washington v. Bash
questions: Whether RCW 16.08.100(3), which makes an owner guilty of a class C felony if the owner's dog "aggressively attacks and causes severe injury or death of any human," sets forth a strict liability crime, and, if so, whether the trial court erred in holding that an affirmative defense to the crime exists if the owner neither knew nor should have known the dog was dangerous.

title: State of Washington v. Cronin
questions: Whether leaving a death penalty notice with the receptionist at defense counsel's office constituted proper service of the notice on counsel.

title: State of Washington v. Cooper
questions: Whether the State has jurisdiction over a crime committed by an Indian on Indian property outside the boundaries of an established Indian reservation.

title: State of Washington v. Graham
questions: Whether an off-duty police officer, working as a private security guard but wearing a police uniform, is a public servant engaged in official duties for purposes of the crimes of obstructing a public servant and resisting arrest.

title: State of Washington v. Stephen B. Pick
questions: Did the trial court err in failing to grant a new trial when, before the verdict was read in open court, the prosecutor discussed with a juror inadmissible evidence regarding the defendant's prior conviction?
